title: Shadowmoon Valley
body: Shadowmoon Valley lies in the far southeast of Outland, a land of ash, black rock and rivers of fel lava under a smoky sky. The orcs of the Shadowmoon clan once honored their ancestors here, and the draenei raised the Temple of Karabor, one of their holiest sites. Both were lost: Gul'dan's warriors took Karabor, and the warlock raised the volcano at the valley's center in a ritual that severed the orcs from the elements. The temple is now Illidan Stormrage's throne, and his servants hold the valley in his name.

title: Wildhammer Stronghold
body: Wildhammer Stronghold stands in the southwest of the valley, the fortress of Kurdran Wildhammer, thane of the Wildhammer in Outland, credited in the Second War with slaying nine dragons and mourned on Azeroth as dead for twenty years. Infernals fall on its walls from Legion Hold, and the ground itself is restless: the stronghold was built over the ancestral grounds of the Shadowmoon orcs, whose spirits, dormant for nearly twenty years, now wander its courtyards.

title: Shadowmoon Village
body: Shadowmoon Village is the Horde's outpost in the northwest of the valley, held by Overlord Or'barokh and the elite Kor'kron guard. It lives under the Legion's guns, infernals raining on its walls from Legion Hold, and it is haunted as well: the chief apothecary warns that the land is full of ghosts, and crafts goggles to reveal the spirits drifting among the buildings.

title: Legion Hold
body: Legion Hold is the Burning Legion's fortress in western Shadowmoon, where it stocks and prepares the infernals that pound both outposts. Between the outposts the Shadow Council works the Deathforge, a foundry where infernals are made as fast as the Legion can hurl them, and the hold's mo'arg labor over a rare ore etched with glowing runes.

parts.body: Spies at the hold's communication device heard the war's direction: an image of Warbringer Razuun, speaking for Doom Lord Kazzak, ordering both strongholds destroyed.

title: The Hand of Gul'dan
body: The Hand of Gul'dan is the great volcano at the center of the valley, raised by the warlock in the ritual that tore the orcs away from the elements. On its western outskirts stands the Altar of Damnation, where Gul'dan spoke the words that shattered this land, and a memory of him still stands there among the kneeling spirits of the damned, while shaman of the Earthen Ring try to commune with the tortured elements.

parts.body: The spirits name Cyrukh the Firelord, an elemental lord unearthed by Gul'dan's ritual, who can be called forth only by the ritual's own words.
sources: quest 10568 description (Gul'dan raised the volcano, Baa'ri buried under lava)

parts.body: Those words are the Cipher of Damnation. Kept for twenty years in Gul'dan's quarters inside Karabor, they were found by Illidan when he took the temple and split among his servants.

title: Oronok's Farm
body: High on the Shattered Shelf above Coilskar Cistern, a weathered orc keeps a campfire and a herd of trained felboars that root tubers out of the hard earth of the plains below. He calls himself Oronok Torn-heart, hermit and farmer, invites travelers to warm themselves by his fire, and advises those who ask after words of damnation to let the dead rest.

parts.body: Oronok was a lieutenant of Gul'dan and stood at the Altar of Damnation when the land was shattered. Sick at heart, he fled to the hills with his three sons, and it took him twenty years to reach the elements again.
sources: quest 10513 log text (Shattered Shelf, north of Coilskar Cistern)

parts.body: His youngest, Ar'tor, died at Illidari Point hunting a piece of the cipher, and sent word from beyond that he died free and waits for his father in the hunting grounds.

title: Akama
body: Akama leads the Ashtongue, the most feared tribe of the Broken. At Illidan's command his people dig in the Ruins of Baa'ri for the relics buried there, and his Deathsworn hold the Warden's Cage, a prison rumored to be a torture chamber. To the Aldor and the Scryers he is evil and cunning; to many of his own people he is a traitor and Illidan's lapdog, and Akama says it is best that they go on thinking so, for now.

parts.body: He serves Illidan only in appearance, bound by visions that foretold his race's destruction otherwise, and in a hidden chamber of the Warden's Cage he keeps Maiev Shadowsong, the Warden who hunted Illidan to Outland.
sources: npc_text 10447 (known as a traitor, Illidan's lapdog)

parts.body: Holding the Heart of Fury, an ata'mal crystal, he felt the power he once saw Velen wield and was tempted to rule Outland with it. That was not his vision, and he sent it to A'dal.

title: The Black Temple
body: The Black Temple was once the Temple of Karabor, the great sanctuary of the draenei. Gul'dan's Horde took it, the Shadow Council made it their seat, and later the pit lord Magtheridon ruled from it, until Illidan drove him out with the help of Akama's Broken. Before its walls Illidan trains blood elf demon hunters in the Ruins of Karabor, and the naaru Xi'ri gathers the Aldor and the Scryers on the approach.

parts.body: The ghosts of Karabor's clerics, murdered by Teron Gorefiend after the city fell, still roam before its walls, where the fel orcs of the Shadowmoon clan hold the holy Ata'mal Terrace.

parts.body: Varedis, who runs the training grounds, was one of five blood elves Kael'thas sent to Illidan. He alone survived, surpassed his masters within a year and learned by heart the Book of Fel Names.

title: Netherwing Fields
body: East of the Hand of Gul'dan, fields of enormous blue crystals jut from the earth and nether drakes wheel above them, too afraid of the Dragonmaw to come down even to feed. On the fields' eastern edge rises Dragonmaw Fortress, where the clan tortures captured drakes until they bend. Past the fields, a lonely shrine called the Altar of Shadows is said to hold the spirit of an ancient Shadowmoon orc.

parts.body: The restless spirits of Shadowmoon whisper one name: Teron Gorefiend, the warlock whose soul Gul'dan placed in the body of a slain Stormwind knight, the first death knight of the Horde.
sources: quest 10481 description (fields of gigantic blue crystals)

parts.body: The Altar of Shadows is no shrine but a prison, and the ancient spirit within it is Teron Gorefiend himself.

title: Netherwing Ledge
body: Netherwing Ledge was once part of the Shadowmoon mainland; now it floats in the sky off the valley's southeastern shelf. It was the Netherwing's sanctuary until the Dragonmaw took it, and Overlord Mor'ghor drives peons and Murkblood Broken to strip its crystals and ore for Illidan's armies. Above it the drake Vhel'kur, spawn of Deathwing, flies an endless circle around the island that was his home and is now his grave.

parts.body: The waking of the sleeping dragon in its mines was no accident: the Netherwing offered the Murkblood peace, and the Broken helped make the mine unlivable for the Dragonmaw.

title: Eclipse Point
body: Eclipse Point is a terraced ruin in the south of the valley, held by the Eclipsion, blood elves in Illidan's service, and on the Path of Conquest to its east they muster soldiers and cavaliers for a great advance, courting the giants of Shadowmoon to their side. At the path's southern end stands Crimson Watch, where the High General of the Sha'tar floats inside a crystal prison.

parts.body: His jailers are the Crimson Sigil, Illidan's elite, at the top of the chain of command for every Illidari force outside the Black Temple, who speak directly with the Betrayer.
